reason: This passage from Genesis 41 extensively describes and emphasizes the establishment of hierarchical authority structures. The text explicitly details Joseph's elevation to power with repeated affirmations of his authority: Pharaoh states 'you shall be over my house, and all my people shall obey you' (וְעַל־פִּ֖יךָ יִשַּׁ֣ק כָּל־עַמִּ֑י), and 'without you, no one shall lift hand or foot in all the land of Egypt' (וּבִלְעָדֶ֗יךָ לֹֽא־יָרִ֨ים אִ֧ישׁ אֶת־יָד֛וֹ וְאֶת־רַגְל֖וֹ). Joseph is given symbols of authority (Pharaoh's ring, fine linen, gold chain), placed in 'the second chariot' (explicitly denoting rank), and people are directed to obey his commands. The narrative culminates with all Egypt coming to Joseph for aid, reinforcing his position in the power structure.
